insulin_sufficiency.summary: Overall insulin delivery shows opportunity for improvement (TIR 64%, TBR<70 0.8%, TAR>180 35%). 1 risk(s) identified; 2 parameter change(s) proposed this cycle.

basal.evidence: Deconfounded basal block audit (EXP-3447): morning 6:00-12:00 has 2017 clean samples after inferred-meal exclusion, median glucose 152 mg/dL, TBR 0.0%, and Loop actual/scheduled basal median 1.41 with additions >115% in 74% of samples.
basal.justification: Basal increase: implement the practical step 0.85 -> 0.94 (+11%) now. Theoretical optimum is 0.94 (+11%); the practical step honors a safe titration cap of 20% per cycle. This derives from a validated deconfounded estimate (the controller-masking confound is already removed), so it is not down-weighted for controller masking. Increase basal by 10% during morning (6:00-12:00). This is a narrow deconfounded step: inferred-meal windows are excluded, Loop is consistently adding basal, and TBR is below 4%. Use the 2-week TBR guardrail before considering another step.

success: TIR improves by at least +0.5 pp toward the projected 65% within 2 weeks.
TBR<70 does not worsen by more than 1 pp.
stop_escalate: TBR<70 increases by more than 1 pp after the Basal change -> revert and escalate.
No measurable TIR improvement at 2 weeks -> reassess direction.

isf.summary: ISF: no change recommended (insufficient evidence (confidence 0.35 below 0.50)).
isf.evidence: Demand-phase ISF (EXP-2651): true 0–2h insulin effect ≈ 25.3 mg/dL/U, 95% CI 17.7–32.9 from 7 correction(s), confidence=low, vs profile 45. Apparent/correction ISF 74.3 is 2.9× inflated by AID compensation and is NOT the target.
isf.justification: ISF reviewed: a directional signal exists (theoretical target 25.3) but is held due to insufficient evidence (confidence 0.35 below 0.50). Re-evaluate at the next review.

success: ISF held: glycemic metrics remain within tolerance of baseline over the 2-week window.
No new hypoglycemia signal (TBR<70 stays below 4%).
stop_escalate: TBR<70 rises by more than 1 pp -> escalate review.
TIR declines materially -> re-open ISF for change.

cr.evidence: Consolidated from 4 time-block advisories (range: 6-29%). Context-aware CR analysis (EXP-2341): morning meals show mean excursion 55 mg/dL from 55 meals.
cr.justification: Carb ratio decrease: implement the practical step 10.5 -> 9.7 (-8%) now. Theoretical optimum is 9.7 (-8%); the practical step honors a safe titration cap of 20% per cycle. Decrease morning CR from 10.5 to 9.7 g/U (7% more insulin). Mean post-meal excursion is 55 mg/dL.

success: TIR improves by at least -4.0 pp toward the projected 56% within 2 weeks.
TBR<70 does not worsen by more than 1 pp.
stop_escalate: TBR<70 increases by more than 1 pp after the Carb ratio change -> revert and escalate.
No measurable TIR improvement at 2 weeks -> reassess direction.

overall_justification: Practical changes this cycle: Basal 0.85->0.94; Carb ratio 10.5->9.7. Each practical step is the safe-titration projection of a larger theoretical optimum (documented in the addenda). Held/deferred: ISF (insufficient_evidence).
addenda: Factors considered: time-in-range distribution, hypo/hyper burden, glycemic variability, per-parameter advisory evidence, and cross-parameter sequencing.
Basal theoretical optimum: 0.94 (+11% vs current 0.85); practical step capped at 20%/cycle -> 0.94.
ISF theoretical optimum: 25.3 (-44% vs current 45); held this cycle.
Carb ratio theoretical optimum: 9.7 (-8% vs current 10.5); practical step capped at 20%/cycle -> 9.7.
Risks reviewed and mitigated: Hyperglycemia burden elevated (TAR>180 34.9% vs target 25%).

Deconfounding applied: Basal recommendation(s) derive from validated deconfounded estimates (e.g. demand-phase ISF EXP-2651, correction-denominator/bilateral EXP-2741, deconfounded basal EXP-3447). The controller-masking confidence penalty does not apply to these, improving accuracy without removing the controller's residual safety margin (EXP-2738).

Mitigations: changes are bounded by a per-cycle titration cap; carb ratio is sequenced after basal/ISF to avoid confounded adjustment; explicit stop/escalate criteria accompany every recommendation for the 2-week feedback loop.

Dose-shaping guidance (ISF, NOT a baseline schedule change): Correction doses above 1.5U show diminishing returns. At 4.1U, each unit achieves only 13 mg/dL drop vs 45 mg/dL at 1U. Consider: (1) splitting large corrections into smaller doses spaced 30+ min apart, (2) using ISF=13 for doses ≥4U. This is a pharmacokinetic property (β=0.9), not circadian. This describes a dose-conditional effective value for large corrections; prefer splitting large corrections over altering the baseline ISF schedule.

reboot.rationale: Settings reboot not indicated: the severe-mismatch composite (burden + large mismatch + low consistency) is not met. Incremental titration is appropriate.

figures.title: Time-in-range distribution
figures.caption: Share of time in each glycemic band over 25,758 readings. Green is the 70-180 mg/dL target; reds are lows, ambers are highs.
figures.alt: Stacked bar of time spent in each glucose range.

figures.title: Ambulatory glucose profile (AGP)
figures.caption: Median glucose by time of day with interquartile (25–75%) and 10–90% bands. The green zone is the 70–180 mg/dL target; a flat median inside it is the goal.
figures.alt: Ambulatory glucose profile percentile bands by hour of day.

figures.title: Overnight glucose profile (00:00–06:00)
figures.caption: Median overnight glucose with IQR. A rising trend suggests basal is too low; a falling trend suggests it is too high. Used to contextualize the basal recommendation.
figures.alt: Overnight median glucose by hour with interquartile band.

figures.title: Post-meal glucose excursion
figures.caption: Median glucose rise after 189 carb-counted, bolused meals (peak +60 mg/dL at 155 min; +28 mg/dL vs baseline at 4 h). Recommendation: decrease carb ratio 10.5→9.7 g/U to tighten meal coverage and lower these peaks.
figures.alt: Mean post-meal glucose excursion curve with interquartile band.

figures.title: Demand-phase ISF decomposition
figures.caption: Profile ISF vs the apparent/correction ISF (amplified by AID compensation) vs the demand-phase ISF — the validated 0–2h insulin effect (EXP-2651) and the true target, shown with its 95% confidence interval. The apparent value is not the target; the recommendation tracks the demand-phase value, bounded by a safety margin (EXP-2738).
figures.alt: Bar chart of profile, apparent, and demand-phase ISF with CI.

figures.title: Scheduled vs actual basal
figures.caption: Median programmed basal vs what the loop actually delivered by hour. Persistent loop deviation indicates the scheduled rate is mismatched in that direction.

figures.title: ISF reconciliation (profile vs observed)
figures.caption: Profile ISF vs the correction-derived (observed/apparent) ISF. The observed value is amplified by AID compensation (basal suspension during corrections), so it is NOT a direct ISF target: the recommendation deliberately preserves the controller's residual safety margin (EXP-2738) rather than chasing the apparent value. Separately, a lower effective ISF for large single corrections is dose-shaping guidance (split the dose), not a baseline schedule change.
